 Opportunity
 20/10/2026 11.00 - CET

 EIT
 The EIT Higher Education Initiative Call is now open!
 The call is offering up to €1.25 million per project over 18 months, with a total budget of €40 million, to strengthen innovation and entrepreneurship capacity in higher education, focusing on manufacturing and deep tech. It will support projects that help universities develop innovation and entrepreneurship skills, improve technology transfer services and build stronger links with businesses. 
 Projects will focus on three key areas: 
 - STEM talent for innovation and entrepreneurship: Developing innovation, entrepreneurship and intellectual property skills among students and staff in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and related fields. 
- Institutional capacity for knowledge valorisation and innovation: Strengthening universities' ability to turn research and knowledge into innovations, including through improved technology transfer, intellectual property management and support for startups. 
- Integration into innovation ecosystems: Building stronger links between higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, investors and innovation networks, particularly in manufacturing and deep tech. 
 Eligibility and consortium requirements 
 Who can apply?
 To be eligible, consortia must meet the following requirements:
 - Consortium composition: Each consortium must include at least five funded partners: at least three HEIs (from three different Horizon Europe-eligible countries, including at least one EU Member State) and at least two business/industry partners and/or business/industry representative organisations (e.g. SMEs, startups, larger enterprises and industry associations). Industry partners operating in manufacturing or deep-tech technologies are strongly encouraged to join a consortium. 
- Eligibility: Organisations funded under the EIT HEI Call 2025 are not eligible to apply under the 2026 call. Each organisation may participate as a funded beneficiary in only one 2026 call application. 
 How to apply 
 Consortia of higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, public bodies and other non-academic partners can prepare their applications by consulting the full  call text   and finding potential partners through the  matchmaking platform . 
 Selected projects will be announced later in 2027.

Catalyse NEB 2027 Open Call
 Opportunity
 29/10/2026 14.00 - CET 
 15/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 Grow your startup with the New European Bauhaus
 Catalyse NEB is the EIT Community New European Bauhaus (NEB) accelerator for startups integrating sustainability, aesthetics and inclusion into their businesses, products and services.
 The New European Bauhaus is an EU initiative that aims to make places and ways of living more sustainable, inclusive and beautiful.
 The programme will support 20 startups that address community needs in areas related to climate, food or urban mobility.
 How it works   
 Each selected startup receives a €22 000 grant and tailored business support, including:    
 - tailored one-to-one business and design mentoring;   
 - workshops covering business development, communications and New European Bauhaus values;   
 - online and in-person networking activities; 
 - visibility opportunities throughout the programme.   
 Who can apply?   
 Both EIT KIC partners and non-partners may apply. Applicants must:   
 - be a for-profit startup incorporated after 1 January 2022 in an eligible country: an EU Member State, a linked Overseas Country or Territory, or a third country associated to Horizon Europe Pillar 3; 
 - have a registered Participant Identification Code at the time of application; 
 - have generated at least €15 000 in revenue in 2026, secured at least €40 000 in investment, or participated in Ignite NEB; 
 - have received, or be seeking, venture funding and be at pre-seed, seed or, exceptionally, Series A stage, with no more than €1 million raised in total; 
 - have a Technology/Business Readiness Level of at least 4, or have participated in Ignite NEB; 
 - have more than 50% of shares owned by the founder and/or co-founders; 
 - meet at least ambition level 1 for each of the three NEB core values, as defined in the NEB Compass ;
 - address at least one strategic focus area of a participating KIC.   
 How to apply   
 Complete the application form , select at least one strategic focus area, and submit:   
 - Proof of incorporation.   
 - Proof of revenue or investment received, except for Ignite NEB applicants.   
 - A pitch deck.   
 For questions, contact neb@eitcommunity.eu .

Resilience Roadmaps
 Opportunity
 25/11/2026 17.00 - CET 
 27/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 Creativity
 EIT Culture & Creativity has announced €1.275 million in funding for Resilience Roadmaps to support ten projects that will translate Europe’s environmental and societal transitions into lasting local change. 
 The ten projects will bring cultural organisations, communities and public authorities together to tackle challenges affecting people and places across Europe. Over 18 months, each project will work with at least 65 community participants, applying cultural, artistic and design practices to co-create a Resilience Roadmap: a living plan that turns locally defined solutions into a clear course for future action, facilitating uptake by public authorities and providing a pathway for wider application. 
 From ten roadmaps to a European body of practice 
 The projects will work across three dimensions of resilience: 
 - Intergenerational fairness: focusing on dialogue and shared decision-making across generations 
- Climate justice: focusing on fair responses to environmental change 
- Community cohesion: focusing on strengthening trust, inclusion and collective responses to shared challenges 
 Acting as future-making laboratories, the ten projects will apply cultural practices, creative approaches and design to prototype solutions across different social, geographical and institutional contexts, showing what can be adapted elsewhere, what depends on local conditions and what enables successful approaches to endure. 
 Taken together, the resulting roadmaps will form a European body of practice, creating transferable knowledge and approaches for cities, regions, cultural organisations and policymakers facing similar challenges. Crucially, they will provide evidence of how place-based approaches can move from local experimentation into sustained public practice. 
 How to apply 
 The Resilience Roadmaps call will provide up to €127 500 per project over 18 months. Projects must be led by a cultural or creative organisation and include at least one public authority. 
 A dedicated information session for applicants will be held on 15 December from 15:30 to 17:00 CET. 
 Find the full call details and register for the info session here

data.title: Growth Projects
data.desc: What are Growth Projects?  BASS Growth Projects are a new funding framework designed to help space-enabled solutions that have already achieved demonstrable commercial success in a primary market to unlock secondary market opportunities.  The scope of Growth Projects includes the development, integration and testing of new service elements to meet the requirements of secondary markets, as well as the implementation of large-scale pilots.  Who are Growth Projects for? ESA BASS Growth Projects are aimed at ambitious companies or industrial teams which have developed a space-enabled solution that has already been validated in the primary market. This funding opportunity is intended as a springboard for business growth by supporting expansion into new markets.  What we offer   ESA funding personalised support from a member of the ESA team  the use of the ESA brand for credibility Optional Support: Some companies applying for Growth Projects may not yet have a fully established ecosystem to commercialise their solution at scale and may need to expand their network of partners. For this reason, the Growth Project framework offers optional support to assist companies with establishing strategic partnerships, expanding the value chain, enabling access to global markets and managing the business risks associated with the identified market opportunities. This will be done by connecting applicants with strategic players from the Growth Projects Partner Network. This network, established by ESA, brings together business multipliers, investors, accelerators, consultancies, users, customers, and data or asset providers, with the objective of fostering strategic partnerships that strengthen the value chain, facilitate access to global markets, and mitigate business risks by connecting projects with organisations able to provide relevant expertise, resources, or market access.  If your company can provide some of the support described above, scroll further down for more information. The optional support includes access to: the Growth Projects Partner Network ESA BASS Task Forces business coaching, matchmaking and exposure opportunities networking and dedicated events How much funding is available? Please see the detailed co-funding rules below:   Growth Projects Activity Cost case by case assessment (limited to eligible cost) ESA Co-funding   Baseline up to 50% of eligible cost Micro, small and medium enterprises up to 80% of eligible cost Universities, research institutes, the public sector (without commercial interest) up to 100% of eligible cost with ESA co-funding not exceeding 30% of the total activity cost Universities, research institutes, the public sector (with commercial interest) up to 75% of eligible cost Industry co-funding remaining costs required to carry out the activity. Co-funding can be provided through the public or private sector, directly or indirectly Please note that funding participation is open to groups, organisations and businesses that reside in ESA member states that have subscribed to BASS. Currently these countries are Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. How to apply for a Growth Project To start the application process you will first need to create an account on ESA's Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP). The application process follows a standard three-step process: Growth Project Questionnaire (GPQ) > Outline Proposal > Full Proposal Within the GPQ form, the company can indicate areas of support required at the point of submission. Once the GPQ step has successfully passed to the next stage, ESA will support when possible by, for example, facilitating introductions with members of the Growth Projects Partner Network.  Please note that a Written Authorisation for ESA Funding must be submitted together with the Full Proposal – applicants are advised to contact their National Delegation(s) as early as possible in the process to obtain one. Apply for a Growth Project Are you interested in joining the Growth Projects Partner Network? We are inviting expressions of interest from investors, accelerators, consultancies, business multipliers, and organisations interested in collaborating, testing, or adopting emerging space-enabled services. By joining this network, you will gain access to future matchmaking opportunities designed to connect relevant partners and support collaboration across the space-enabled ecosystem. Investors: It is a high-level objective for ESA to foster commercialisation of and private investment in the European Space industry. As part of this network, investors have early visibility and access to Growth Project candidates. Accelerators, Consultancies and Business Multipliers: Accelerators, consultancies and business multipliers are invited to participate in future exchanges and matchmaking events to support Growth Project candidates establish strategic partnerships, expand their value chain, enable access to global markets and manage the business risks.  Organisations interested in supporting Growth Projects as users or customers: ESA will be supporting Growth Project candidates with matchmaking to users and customers whenever this is required. Companies willing to collaborate can benefit from: early access to innovative space-based solutions entering new markets opportunities to co-develop or test services within large-scale pilots participation in matchmaking activities organised by ESA BASS building strategic relationships with innovative European companies Companies interested in supporting Growth Projects as technology, data or asset providers: If your organisation has some technology, data or assets you’d like to provide to support Growth Projects, we would like to hear from you. Express interest in joining the Growth Projects Partner Network   Disclaimer Please note that all information provided on this webpage is for general guidance only. In case of any discrepancies or conflicts, the official ESA sources shall always take precedence. These include, but are not limited to: •    esa-star publication •    esa-star tendering Participants are strongly advised to refer to these official channels for authoritative and up-to-date information regarding ESA opportunities, requirements, and procedures.

data.title: Space for Smart Tourism
data.countryText: Belgium, Canada, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland
data.desc: The Opportunity   Tourism is one of Europe's most important economic sectors, contributing significantly to employment, regional development and economic growth. Following the recovery of international travel since COVID-19, destinations across Europe are experiencing increasing visitor numbers while facing growing pressure to manage tourism sustainably, enhance visitor experiences and protect natural and cultural assets.  Destinations, tourism operators and public authorities are looking for innovative digital solutions that support more efficient tourism management, improve visitor services and help balance economic growth with environmental and social sustainability. Challenges such as overtourism, seasonal demand fluctuations, congestion, accessibility, environmental impact and changing traveller expectations require new approaches supported by reliable data and real-time insights.  At the same time, visitors increasingly expect personalised, seamless and digital experiences before, during and after their trips. Meanwhile, tourism stakeholders require better tools to understand visitor flows, monitor destinations, optimise infrastructure, improve safety and support informed decision-making.  Topics of relevance  Visitor flow monitoring and management  Services that monitor and forecast visitor movements, identify congestion and help distribute visitors more effectively. Solutions could include dynamic routing, congestion alerts and decision-support tools for destination managers.   Sustainable tourism and environmental monitoring  Solutions that help destinations and tourism operators assess and reduce their environmental impact. Applications could include monitoring environmental pressures, land-use or coastal changes and emissions, as well as supporting sustainability reporting, responsible destination planning and regenerative tourism models.   Smart cultural and natural heritage management  Services supporting the monitoring and protection of cultural and natural heritage sites. Applications could include site-condition assessment, risk detection, visitor-impact analysis and digital models supporting conservation and long-term asset management.   Seamless mobility and travel experience  Integrated services that make it easier for visitors to combine different transport modes, particularly when accessing rural, remote or less-connected destinations. Applications could include multimodal travel planning, accessibility routing and improved first- and last-mile connectivity.   Immersive and inclusive tourism experiences  Location-based digital services that improve access to cultural and natural assets. These could include augmented and virtual reality experiences, accessible navigation for people with disabilities, digital interpretation tools and remote tourism experiences.   Safety, resilience and crisis support  Services helping travellers, tourism operators and destinations respond to natural hazards, environmental events and operational disruptions. Applications could include situational awareness, location-based alerts, emergency communications and crisis decision-support tools.   Remote connectivity for rural and remote destinations  Connectivity solutions enabling tourism services in areas with limited terrestrial coverage. Applications could support rural tourism businesses, online bookings, digital guest services, Internet of Things monitoring and access to real-time travel and safety information.  Value of Space  Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS)  GNSS can provide precise positioning for visitor flow analysis, navigation, mobility services and accessible routing. It can support the monitoring of visitor movements, helping tourism destinations understand how visitors move between locations, and manage visitor flows more effectively. GNSS can also enable location-based tourism experiences, including digital services that provide information or content according to the visitor’s location. Geofencing, tracking and safety functions can further support visitor management and improve mobility across tourism destinations.   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO)  SatEO can provide data for environmental monitoring, land-use and coastal-change detection, and the assessment of natural and cultural assets. It can support destinations and tourism operators in monitoring environmental pressures associated with tourism activities and understanding changes affecting sensitive locations. SatEO can also contribute to sustainability indicators, environmental impact assessments and evidence-based destination planning. These capabilities can support the protection and long-term management of natural and cultural heritage, as well as the development of more sustainable and responsible tourism.   Satellite Communications (SatCom)  SatCom can provide connectivity in remote or poorly served areas where terrestrial infrastructure may be insufficient. This can enable digital services for travellers and tourism businesses, including online bookings, digital guest services and access to real-time travel and safety information. SatCom can also support IoT monitoring networks, emergency communications and remote access to digital content. By providing connectivity where terrestrial services are limited or disrupted, SatCom can contribute to the operational continuity and resilience of tourism services in rural, peripheral and hard-to-reach destinations.  What we look for We invite submissions of early-stage service concepts that address customer needs, show commercial potential and technical feasibility, and leverage satellite data or space technology. Kick-starts should be led by experienced, motivated teams, with a clear ambition and a credible pathway to developing commercially viable services. What we offer We offer funding and support to companies, specifically to help teams carry out a feasibility study over a six-month period. During this time, teams can develop their business case, work on technical aspects, validating the integration of satellite data and space technologies into the proposed solution, and engage actively with users and customers.  We offer:  75% funding from the European Space Agency to a maximum of €75,000 for each selected study, provided on a zero-equity basis. The total cost per study is up to €100,000.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network and partners  Use of the ESA brand for your service  Please note that we do not provide direct access to space data, nor are we responsible for the space segment of service development. Applicants should have a clear plan for how they will obtain any required space data and ensure they have the necessary expertise within their team to help manage this aspect.  Who can apply? This opportunity is open to companies that intend to develop space-enabled services and products related, but not restricted, to the topics of relevance outlined above. This opportunity is open to companies that intend to develop space-enabled services and products related, but not restricted, to the topics of relevance outlined above. To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland. Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Latvia, Malta, Norway, Slovakia and United Kingdom are not supporting this call. Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) as soon as possible and to apply for a Written Authorisation for ESA funding.  Webinar To find out more and for your opportunity to ask questions, join us for a one-hour webinar on 25 November, 11:00 CET. Register now How to apply 1.    Register your team on esa-star registration. 2.    When the Kick-start opens find it on esa-star publication and download the official competition documents. 3.    Use the official documents to prepare your proposal. 4.    Reach out to your National Delegate(s) to apply for a Written Authorisation for ESA Funding.  5.    Submit your proposal via esa-star tendering before the deadline. Disclaimer: Please note that all information provided on this webpage is for general guidance only. In case of any discrepancies or conflicts, the official ESA sources shall always take precedence. These include, but are not limited to:  •    esa-star publication  •    esa-star tendering  Participants are strongly advised to refer to these official channels for authoritative and up-to-date information regarding ESA opportunities, requirements, and procedures.

data.title: Road and Traffic Safety
data.countryText: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom
data.desc: The funding opportunity Road and traffic safety is a critical concern globally. In many regions, rapid urbanisation and the growing number of vehicles have led to increased accidents, amplifying the need for improved traffic management, incident detection, and predictive safety solutions to reduce accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the roads. Also, there is a change in the types of vehicles we see on roads, with increasing presence of micromobility and automated vehicles reshaping existing mobility patterns. These emerging modes of transport require updated safety solutions to ensure that traffic management and infrastructure are adapted accordingly. This opportunity offers funding for teams who would like to develop sustainable space-based services and applications that address challenges related to the Road and Traffic Safety sector. The challenge According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 1.35 million people die each year because of road traffic crashes, making it the leading cause of death for children and young adults aged 5-29 years. In September 2020, the UN General Assembly proclaimed the Decade of Action for Road Safety, with the ambitious target of preventing at least 50% of road traffic deaths and injuries by 2030. European governments continue to monitor progress towards this target, regularly updating standards and encouraging the ‘safety first’ mentality such as the use of seat belts and helmets.  Industry is also actively working on improving safety of both vehicles and the surrounding ecosystem. With the rise of digital, connected and autonomous mobility solutions, there is enormous potential for improved safety through reduced human error and improved information sharing. New services at the intersection of these trends have the potential to drastically improve the safety of roads and bring scalable benefits. The market is projected to grow, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence, IoT sensors and cloud computing, allowing for greater accuracy, scalability and cost-effectiveness of road safety systems. Against this backdrop of increasing risks, evolving mobility patterns and expanding technological opportunities, this proposed Road and Traffic Safety Call for Proposals aims to develop solutions that leverage space-enabled technologies to enhance safety and traffic management, to improve the collection of critical data, and to better protect vulnerable road users, ultimately contributing to the reduction of accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the roads. Topics of relevance This Call for Proposals has been designed in collaboration with ESA BASS partners, who have helped to identify the following use cases. Please note, that these are only examples and the call is not limited to the use cases listed below: Enhancing information exchange Vehicle-to-Vehicle and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication applications could allow vehicles to share information about their speed, position and direction, as well as providing alerts about potential dangers, such as approaching vehicles or hazardous road conditions. This near real-time data exchange can enhance overall road safety of passengers, drivers, cyclists and pedestrians. Improving Road design, signage and maintenance to reduce accidents Well-designed roads with clear signage and better road markings can help drivers navigate safely and support automated vehicles by ensuring they have the necessary references. Regular and proactive road maintenance such as repairing potholes, clearing debris, restoring worn markings, and addressing drainage issues prevents accidents caused by deteriorating road conditions. It can be achieved through:  Rapid detection, prioritisation and repair of road defects, such as potholes, surface cracks, faded markings, or obstructed signage. Designing and planning safer infrastructure to address the needs of pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and paying attention to the specific needs of people with disabilities, children and the elderly. Upgrading existing infrastructure for improved prevention, detection and communication of accidents.  Improving road safety by optimising traffic flow Validation of environmental claims, cross-validation of data and validation of inconsistencies for insurance companies, auditing firms, certifying bodies and corporations. Monitoring traffic flow and congestion helps to identify bottlenecks and areas with high accident rates and allows for dynamic adjustments to traffic signals and other control measures. This can improve the overall efficiency and safety of the road network by reducing traffic jams and alleviating congestion during peak hours. Implementing measures to protect non-motorised road users Implementing measures to protect non-motorised road users and to ensure that pedestrians, micromobility users and cyclists have safe spaces to travel, reducing the risk of accidents. Such measures could involve systems monitoring vulnerable road users' safety and providing alerts about potential dangers, such as approaching vehicles or hazardous road conditions. Improving International Road Assessment Programme (iRAP) survey completion The star-rating protocol, set out by the International Road Assessment Programme (iRAP), is a way to assess how safe roads are. These surveys rely on information about road context, observed traffic flow, and infrastructure attributes to produce risk-based safety ratings. Tools to significantly improve the completion of surveys, through increasing cost-effectiveness, efficiency, frequency and precision are needed. Value of space SatEO imagery can be used to update maps, monitor environmental hazards, and assess the conditions of roads. SatEO is valuable for planning and maintaining road networks, therefore preventing accidents caused by poor road conditions. SatEO data, such as weather nowcasting, can help vehicle systems to adjust the vehicle's speed and trajectory to current road conditions. Finally, SatEO can be used in advanced routing applications to optimise the route based on hazards or weather conditions. SatNav provides accurate positioning, navigation, and timing, which are essential for guiding and navigating vehicles, especially those with autonomous capabilities.  Aggregated GNSS data from connected vehicles, fleets, and mobile devices can be used to monitor traffic flow and to identify congestion patterns. This can improve the overall safety of the road network by reducing traffic jams and congestion during peak hours. SatCom can ensure seamless communication between various systems, enabling near real-time data exchange and coordination.  Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication can leverage Satcom to ensure seamless connectivity in remote areas, therefore playing a significant role in detecting and communicating information about potential hazards. Who can apply? This opportunity is open to companies that intend to develop space-enabled services and products related, but not restricted, to the topics of relevance outlined above.   To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom. For companies based in Denmark, please note that the conditions and timeline specified in the Authorisation of Funding (AoF), available under the “Who can apply?” section of the “Open Call for Proposals: Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects”, apply and take precedence over the information provided in this page. How to apply   Visit the How to Apply to Proof-of-concept studies and Pilot Projects page for the full application details.  Further information and important documentation can be found on the BASS documents page.   Please note that these pages are updated regularly. data.countryText: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and United Kingdom
data.desc: The Opportunity The Smart and Resilient Energy Systems Call for Proposals aims to develop operational solutions using space-enabled technologies to improve the anticipatory, operational, and strategic resilience of electricity grids. Solutions should have a strong focus on critical infrastructure protection, climate resilience, and emergency preparedness. The Call has been developed in collaboration with ELES, Slovenia's combined transmission and distribution system operator, and is based on operational requirements and challenges identified by the organisation. These requirements reflect real-world needs associated with forecasting and grid operations, dynamic thermal rating enhancement, asset intelligence, infrastructure monitoring, digital twin integration and situational awareness across electricity networks, and form the foundation for the use cases within this call. This Call for Proposals will accept proposals for Proof-of-Concept Studies and Pilot Projects. Topics of relevance This Call addresses operational challenges identified by ELES and is organised into three complementary solution clusters. Cluster A: Forecasting & Grid Operations Modern electricity networks require increasingly sophisticated forecasting, planning and operational decision-support capabilities to support network stability, renewable integration and resilient system operation. Areas of interest include: Renewable generation forecasting for solar and wind power Load-flow prediction and congestion analysis Contingency planning for unplanned outages Cross-border scheduling and balancing coordination Seasonal and long-term capacity planning Climate and weather risk assessment Strategic outage mitigation planning Solutions should improve operational awareness, forecasting accuracy and decision-support capabilities across transmission and distribution networks while supporting efficient network utilisation and improved resilience. Cluster B: Dynamic Thermal Rating Enhancement ELES operates the SUMO Dynamic Thermal Rating (DTR) system and is seeking improved environmental monitoring and forecasting capabilities to enhance the utilisation of existing transmission infrastructure. Areas of interest include: Enhanced wind speed and wind direction monitoring Ambient temperature and solar irradiance monitoring High-resolution nowcasting and forecasting of environmental parameters at conductor-representative heights Historical environmental analysis and weather model calibration Integration of environmental data into the SUMO DTR system and operational workflows Solutions should improve the spatial resolution, accuracy and timeliness of environmental inputs to Dynamic Thermal Rating calculations, particularly across Alpine and pre-Alpine transmission corridors. Cluster C: Asset Intelligence, Digital Twin & Situational Awareness Electricity network operators require improved visibility of infrastructure condition, environmental threats and operational risks to support effective asset management and resilient network operations. Areas of interest include: Predictive maintenance and anomaly detection Asset prioritisation and vulnerability assessment Digital twin enrichment and automated data integration Natural hazard monitoring Infrastructure condition monitoring Emergency situational awareness Obstacle and encroachment detection Vegetation and corridor monitoring Cross-domain resilience dashboards Smart-grid assessment and future operational planning Solutions should integrate Earth Observation, Artificial Intelligence, advanced analytics and digital-twin capabilities to improve asset intelligence, infrastructure monitoring and operational awareness across the electricity network. Value of Space Space enabled services can significantly enhance electricity grid operations across multiple domains: Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) enables large-scale, near-real-time or latency-dependent monitoring of hazards such as floods, storms, wildfires, landslides, snow and icing events, as well as vegetation encroachment, construction activities and asset surroundings. These capabilities complement local inspections, drone operations, and GIS-based monitoring, while improving crisis awareness, emergency response coordination and long-term climate resilience planning. When combined with advanced analytics and AI techniques, EO data can also support predictive maintenance, asset prioritisation and digital-twin enrichment, enabling a shift from reactive to risk-based operations. Satellite Communications (SatCom) enables ubiquitous connectivity to enhance communication links, connectivity of IoT devices and networks of sensors, in remote locations. SatCom also provides real-time, long-range communications with infrastructure monitoring systems (i.e. UAVs/robots), enabling remote operation while assisting enabling technologies such as digital twins. Satellite Navigation (SatNav) supports precise asset localisation, time synchronisation for digital operational systems and secure backup communications during emergency or degraded terrestrial network conditions. These services can enhance operational continuity and coordination during large-scale disruptions or crisis events. Satellite enhanced forecasting improves the spatial and temporal resolution of weather driven inputs (solar irradiance, wind fields, ambient temperature), directly supporting renewable generation forecasting, load flow prediction, and dynamic thermal rating. What we are looking for  We look for motivated teams with established business, financial and technical expertise who can address our focus areas with market-ready concepts. Submitted proposals must demonstrate:  Commercial Viability and Sustainable Business Models: Service concepts designed for long-term commercial profitability. Projects targeting public sector or law enforcement users (B2G) are strongly encouraged to incorporate commercial B2B customer streams to ensure post-project sustainability.  Operational Readiness over Research: A clear focus on deploying pre-operational commercial services rather than pure academic research or basic scientific data exploration. Concepts must be driven by practical market demand and active user support.  Technical Data Self-Sufficiency: Bidding teams must already possess the internal technical capability to acquire and process downstream space data. Teams must be self-sufficient from the outset, as ESA provides financial and strategic backing rather than direct software engineering support.  Distinct Space Added Value: Clear, measurable operational or commercial advantages derived directly from the integration of space assets over traditional terrestrial alternatives.  What we offer  Zero-equity co-funding: up to 50–80% of your activity costs, depending on SME status and Member State approval.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network, partners and Taskforce members  ESA brand credibility  Who can apply? To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and United Kingdom.   Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) of the countries where their industrial partners (Prime and Subcontractors) are located as soon as possible.  A Written Authorisation for ESA funding from the National Delegation(s) is required for the Full Proposal.  This call is pre-authorised by Slovenia, which has made funding available for the call. Entities residing in Slovenia do not need to provide dedicated Letters of Authorisation from their National Delegation, subject to the conditions stated in the attached Authorisation of Funding (AoF). For companies based in Denmark, please note that the conditions and timeline specified in the Authorisation of Funding (AoF), available under the “Who can apply?” section of the “Open Call for Proposals: Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects”, apply and take precedence over the information provided in this page. How to apply  Visit the How to Apply to Proof-of-concept studies and Pilot Projects page for the full application details.  The call opens for submissions on 29 September 2026 and closes on 27 November 2026. This closing date refers strictly to the deadline for submitting the initial Activity Pitch Questionnaire (APQ) via the Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP). It does not apply to the subsequent Outline Proposal or Full Proposal stages.  Proposals are assessed individually on a rolling, non-competitive basis; companies are therefore strongly encouraged to submit their APQ as early as possible.  Further information and important documentation can be found on the esa-star publication page and on the BASS documents page.

data.title: Wildfires
data.countryText: Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom and Canada
data.desc: A new call focusing on Wildfire Preparedness opened on 1 September 2026. The earlier Wildfire Response call closed on 2 June 2026. Introduction This is part of the Wildfire Safety initiative, inviting proposals for innovative services that advance wildfire management using space technology and data. The first call focused on Wildfire Response, supporting solutions for early detection of wildfires, near-real-time fire evolution monitoring, and fire behaviour simulation and prediction. A subsequent call focusing on Wildfire Preparedness will open on 1 September 2026, and will address wildfire risk assessment, fuel load management, and the application of preventative and adaptation measures. Challenges Wildfires have forever played an integral role in regulating our natural environment; shaping landscapes and sustaining ecosystems. However, in recent years, the frequency and intensity of wildfires in Europe’s Southern Mediterranean region, as well as parts of Central and Eastern Europe, have notably increased. Data from the European Forest Fires Information System (EFFIS) suggests that the average area affected by fires in 2025 in European Union member states was more than double the average from across 2006-2024. Human activity and environmental conditions favouring wildfire ignition and propagation have historically been the catalysts behind such fires. The extension of urban-forest interfaces, where human settlements and flammable vegetation meet, is exacerbating both the risk of fire onset and the magnitude of their impact. The consequences of such are environmental, economic and social. Wildfires cause extensive loss of, and damage to, lives, natural resources, and property. Local economies suffer due to impacts on tourism, abandonment of rural areas and disruption of trade. The burning of biomass releases pollutants negatively impacting air quality and sowing longer-term impacts on human health and the environment. In parallel, on-going advances in space and terrestrial technologies offer novel means to tackle such challenges. Value of space Satellite data and technology must play a critical role in the solutions proposed for this opportunity. Satellite Earth observation for mapping and monitoring of active fires, burn scars, vegetative health, risk factors, vulnerable infrastructure, and otherwise. Satellite positioning to guide aerial platforms (drones and aircraft) for fire monitoring and suppression, geo-referencing of data collected from aerial platforms and in-situ sensors. Satellite communications to provide connectivity to distributed in-situ sensors across a region, as well as communication links for aerial platforms. What we look for We are looking for motivated teams who can demonstrate credible business and, technical expertise, with promising ideas for space applications that address relevant topics or related areas and demonstrate: credible customer engagement and clearly identified customer needs clear market potential leading to commercially viable service concepts potential technical feasibility with a pathway to implementable solutions clear added value from the use of space data or space-based technologies What we offer zero-equity funding* technical and commercial guidance access to our network and partners ESA brand credibility *(50-80% depending on SME Status and Member State Approval) How to apply Details about how to apply to this call can be found here. Further information and important documentation and guidance around the application process is available here. Please note that these pages are updated regularly. In the unlikely case of contradictory information on different platforms, details published on esa-star take precedence. Authorisation of funding This opportunity is open to companies that intend to develop space-enabled services and products related, but not restricted, to the topics of relevance outlined above. To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom and Canada. Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) of the countries where their industrial partners (Prime and Subcontractors) are located as soon as possible and to apply for a Written Authorisation for ESA funding, as such authorisation is required for the Full Proposal. For companies based in Denmark, please note that the conditions and timeline specified in the Authorisation of Funding (AoF), available under the “Who can apply?” section of the “Open Call for Proposals: Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects”, apply and take precedence over the information provided in this page. data.title: The Arctic Region
data.desc: The Arctic, the most northerly region on Earth, is centred on the North Pole and defined as the area North of the Arctic Circle, 66°N. It is known for its polar night, extensive sea ice, tundra landscape, polar climate and cold adapted ecosystems. It is a region that is also disproportionately impacted by climate change, warming three to four times faster than the global average. The melting ice has led to the Arctic becoming a strategic security zone, as competing global powers vie for control of newly accessible shipping routes and abundant natural resources including oil, gas and rare-earth minerals. Rapid snowmelt threatens towns, roads and industrial infrastructure with flooding, while so-called ‘zombie’ or overwintering wildfires burn year-round in the carbon-rich peat, undetected for extensive periods of time before re-emerging to the surface. Thawing permafrost causes land subsidence, destabilising buildings and releasing greenhouse gases, pollutants and pathogens. The diverse threats facing the Arctic environment, livelihoods, security and economy are expected to become more consequential over time. There is a pressing need to develop solutions to address current and emerging challenges. From maritime safety and surveillance, to search and rescue, defence and security, environmental protection, food security and critical infrastructure protection, the potential for using satellite technologies in innovative solutions is immense. Structure of the Arctic call To address the diversity and complexity of the challenges affecting the Arctic region, this Call for Proposals is composed of three complementary and thematically focused sub‑calls. Each sub‑call targets a specific set of user needs and operational challenges, while sharing a common objective: supporting the development of space‑enabled services that enhance resilience, safety, sustainability and security in the Arctic region. The three sub‑calls are designed to be distinct yet interconnected, reflecting the tight interplay between environmental change, economic activity, maritime operations and geopolitical dynamics. Applicants are encouraged to focus on the sub‑call that best matches their use case and user community. Sub‑call 1 – Environmental and economic resilience This call is now open and closes 4 September 2026 This sub‑call focuses on protecting Arctic ecosystems and supporting climate‑resilient economic activities, with particular attention to fisheries, aquaculture, environmental monitoring, pollution detection and food security. It addresses the growing impact of climate change, increased maritime activity and environmental stressors on both Arctic livelihoods and natural resources. Sub‑call 2 – Safety, navigation and operations This call opens 5 September 2026 and closes 5 November 2026 This sub‑call targets safe maritime navigation and operations in the Arctic, where melting sea ice is not only increasing traffic but also exposing vessels to significant hazards. It addresses challenges related to ice monitoring, route optimisation, search and rescue, situational awareness, and the safe operation of maritime, air and land activities in a remote and infrastructure‑limited environment. Sub‑call 3 – Security and critical protection This call opens 6 November 2026 and closes 6 January 2027 This sub‑call addresses security, sovereignty and protection of critical infrastructure in an increasingly contested region. It focuses on enhancing situational awareness, monitoring unlawful and grey‑zone activities, protecting strategic assets, and supporting Arctic states and allies in responding to growing geopolitical and hybrid threats. What we look for We look for promising business ideas addressing topics of relevance or related areas that propose: attractive market opportunities, identified customer needs and customer engagement commercially-viable service concepts technically feasible solutions added value of space data or technology motivated teams with business, technical and financial expertise What we offer We offer funding and support to companies, both for business case assessment and for the development of new, space-based services. Our offer includes: zero-equity funding* technical and commercial guidance access to our network and partners ESA brand credibility *(50-80% depending on SME Status and Member State Approval) How to apply   The initiative is open to the submission of proposals for: Proof-of-Concept Studies - which provide the preparatory framework to identify, analyse, define and de-risk novel commercially sustainable services Pilot Projects - dedicated to the implementation and demonstration of pre-operational services Proposals must be submitted via the ESA Activity Pitch Questionnaire (APQ). Applicants are encouraged to engage with their National Delegation prior to submission. Please note that the sub-calls listed above have been pre-authorised by the Danish delegation, subject to specific conditions and requirements. Please check the eligibility requirements applicable to Danish companies. Details about how to apply to this call can be found here. Further information and important documentation and guidance around the application process is available here. Please note that these pages are updated regularly. In the unlikely case of contradictory information on different platforms, details published on esa-star take precedence

data.title: The Arctic Region: Security and critical protection
data.desc: The opportunity  This is one of three sub-calls under the Arctic Region Call for Proposals, supporting European space-enabled solutions to address the region's growing operational, environmental and security challenges. Climate change, increasing maritime activity and the growing strategic importance of the Arctic are creating new security and resilience requirements. Critical infrastructure - including ports, energy assets, communication networks and transport corridors - is increasingly exposed to environmental hazards, operational disruptions and malicious activities. Arctic stakeholders require improved capabilities to monitor, protect and respond to emerging threats while maintaining safe and resilient operations across vast and remote territories. This sub-call focuses on security, resilience and critical infrastructure protection. Applications are invited for space-enabled solutions that enhance the monitoring, protection and resilience of critical assets, and support authorities and operators in maintaining security and operational continuity across the Arctic region. Topics of relevance The priority areas below were defined in consultation with Arctic Region stakeholders. Applications are particularly encouraged relating to: critical infrastructure monitoring and protection maritime security and maritime domain awareness detection of anomalous, suspicious or unlawful activities resilience of communication and transport networks emergency preparedness and crisis response cross-border situational awareness and information sharing protection of remote energy, communication and logistics assets Value of Space Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) can provide persistent monitoring of critical infrastructure, maritime activity and remote operational areas. It can support the detection of unusual patterns of activity, the identification of environmental and operational risks, and the monitoring of changes affecting the integrity of infrastructures such as ports, pipelines, communication facilities and transport networks. InSAR techniques can support the monitoring of ground deformation and infrastructure stability, including risks linked to permafrost degradation. Satellite Communications (Satcom) can provide secure and resilient connectivity across remote Arctic regions where terrestrial networks are unavailable or vulnerable. They can support emergency communications, crisis management, command and control functions, and maintain operational continuity during disruptions affecting critical infrastructure and transportation systems. Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) can enable trusted positioning, navigation and timing services for maritime, air and land operations. They can support asset tracking, geofencing, infrastructure monitoring, incident response coordination and the protection of critical transportation and logistics operations across the Arctic. What we look for This sub‑call is open to: Companies (start‑ups, SMEs, large companies) Consortia involving industrial and non‑industrial partners Cross‑sectoral teams combining space and non‑space actors Applicants should demonstrate a clear user need, with users such as public authorities, environmental agencies, fisheries and aquaculture operators, port and coastal authorities, or environmental service providers. What we offer Funding is provided under ESA Business Applications non‑competitive conditions, with co‑funding rates depending on participant profile and Member State contribution. zero-equity funding* technical and commercial guidance access to our network and partners ESA brand credibility *(50-80% depending on SME Status and Member State Approval) How to apply Proposals must be submitted via the ESA Activity Pitch Questionnaire (APQ). Applicants are encouraged to engage with their National Delegation prior to submission. Please note that the sub-calls listed above have been pre-authorised by the Danish delegation, subject to specific conditions and requirements. Please check the eligibility requirements applicable to Danish companies. Full details on how to apply

data.title: Space-Enabled Solutions for Resilient Grids
data.countryText: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom
data.desc: The Opportunity   As energy systems face growing operational, environmental and security challenges, ensuring the resilience of Europe's electricity grids is becoming increasingly important. This is driving demand for innovative solutions that can help grid operators anticipate, detect and respond to disruptions, while maintaining a secure and reliable energy supply.  This Call for Proposals is conducted in collaboration with ENTSO-E, the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity. As part of ESA’s Task Force for Innovation in Energy Through Space, ENTSO-E has consolidated a representative set of generic operational challenges for electricity transmission networks, focusing on system operation, resilience, situational awareness and operational efficiency. The Call invites proposals for Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects for services addressing selected challenges relevant to the resilience and operational continuity of European electricity transmission systems. These include:  growing physical, cyber, and climate-related risks​ to energy infrastructure  increasingly extreme weather events (such as wildfires, floods, storms, heatwaves) affecting grid operations​   increasing dependency on secure infrastructure​ for digitalisation and interconnected power systems, and  economic, societal, and national security impacts from disruption to energy systems  The challenges have been identified through engagement with ENTSO-E and European Transmission System Operators. They are illustrative, intentionally generalised and intended to stimulate innovation. They should not be interpreted as descriptions of the current operational practices, existing capability gaps or specific priorities of ENTSO-E or any individual TSO. Subject to their individual interest and applicable internal, operational, security, regulatory and procurement requirements, participating TSOs may engage with selected bidders as potential users and contribute to the validation and demonstration of proposed solutions. The involvement of ENTSO-E and/or individual TSOs in the development of the thematic scope, use cases, consultations or other activities associated with this Call does not constitute an endorsement, certification, commitment to participate in a pilot, commitment to procure or purchase any solution, or any other contractual or commercial commitment. Any future participation, testing, procurement or deployment by an individual TSO will be subject to its own decision-making processes, applicable legal, regulatory, security, operational and procurement requirements. Topics of Relevance  The use cases are organised under two complementary challenge areas, reflecting the operational needs identified by ENTSO-E in relation to the secure and resilient operation of Europe's interconnected electricity transmission system.  The proposed activities build on existing space-enabled capabilities and services, including Earth observation, positioning, navigation and timing, and satellite communications. The objective is therefore not to develop these capabilities in isolation, but to demonstrate their operational value for TSOs and explore how they can complement existing terrestrial solutions, strengthen resilience and support continuity of grid operations.  The two themes will open for applications one after the other: Theme 1 applications are invited from November 4 2026 to January 29 2027, Theme 2 applications will be invited from February 1 2027 to 30 April 2027. Theme 1 | Situational Awareness for Critical Events  | Opening: 2.11.2026 | Closing: 29.01.2027 Developing solutions that improve the ability of Transmission System Operators to anticipate, detect, understand and assess risks affecting electricity transmission infrastructure and system stability through enhanced awareness of environmental hazards, infrastructure condition and evolving operational risks. Key capabilities:​   Early detection and monitoring of wildfires, floods, extreme weather, and infrastructure failures​  Monitoring of transmission corridors, vegetation encroachment, and environmental risks​  Integration of space weather information for grid risk forecasting​  Post-event damage assessment and operational recovery support​  Scalable and interoperable platforms supporting use across multiple transmission system environments, subject to applicable requirements Theme 2 | Strengthening Operational Resilience for the Grid | Opening: 1.2.2027 | Closing: 30.4.2027 Enhancing the resilience, security and continuity of grid operations through improved operational capabilities, communications, positioning, timing and emergency response services that support effective operation during normal and degraded conditions. Key capabilities:​   High-accuracy and resilient timing capabilities for applications within digital substations and other grid applications requiring stringent timing performance, subject to applicable technical and security requirements ​   Precise positioning for onshore and offshore grid assets​   Detection of interference, spoofing, and signal degradation​   Satellite backup communications when terrestrial networks fail​   Secure connectivity for grid restoration and emergency operations     Value of Space  Space assets provide critical capabilities to support grid resilience:​   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) data can provide valuable capabilities for monitoring infrastructure, environmental risks and to assess damage.   SatEO provides wide-area, persistent monitoring of transmission corridors and substations, enabling near real-time detection and forecasting of wildfires, and supporting rapid flood mapping and post-event damage assessment. SatEO also allows operators to monitor vegetation  encroachment and construction activities that may impact the grid and to detect ground deformation using radar techniques, identifying subsidence or structural movements that could affect critical infrastructure.     Satellite Navigation (SatNav) can provide high-precision positioning capabilities that may support applications within digital sub-stations and other grid assets requiring a stringent synchronisation performance. SatNav can also enable the detection of structural displacement or slow asset movement, and provides independent, resilient timing sources that migrate risks associated with terrestrial timing failures or signal interference.      Satellite Communications (SatCom) support secure and resilient connectivity during outages and emergencies.  SatCom can provide secure backup connectivity during terrestrial network outages or cyber incidents, and enable rapid deployment of communications in disaster-affected areas. It also supports independent command-and-control channels for grid restoration operations, and may support resilient backup communications and interoperability with relevant utility communication environments, subject to the applicable technical, cybersecurity and operational requirements.    Space Weather services can provide valuable capabilities for forecasting and monitoring solar and geomagnetic activity that may impact electricity transmission systems. Space Weather services support the prediction of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) and provide early warning of severe geomagnetic disturbances that may affect grid infrastructure. These capabilities can help operators improve situational awareness, assess potential impacts on critical assets, and support preparedness and mitigation activities before and during space weather events.   Supporting digital technologies including  Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Digital Twins, and advanced data fusion and analytics. What we are looking for  We look for motivated teams with established business, financial and technical expertise who can address our focus areas with market-ready concepts. Submitted proposals must demonstrate:  Commercial Viability and Sustainable Business Models: Service concepts designed for long-term commercial profitability. Projects targeting public sector or law enforcement users (B2G) are strongly encouraged to incorporate commercial B2B customer streams to ensure post-project sustainability.  Operational Readiness over Research: A clear focus on deploying pre-operational commercial services rather than pure academic research or basic scientific data exploration. Concepts must be driven by practical market demand and active user support.  Technical Data Self-Sufficiency: Bidding teams must already possess the internal technical capability to acquire and process downstream space data. Teams must be self-sufficient from the outset, as ESA provides financial and strategic backing rather than direct software engineering support.  Distinct Space Added Value: Clear, measurable operational or commercial advantages derived directly from the integration of space assets over traditional terrestrial alternatives.  What we offer  Zero-equity co-funding: up to 50–80% of your activity costs, depending on SME status and Member State approval.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network, partners and Taskforce members  ESA brand credibility  Who can apply? To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom.   Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) of the countries where their industrial partners (Prime and Subcontractors) are located as soon as possible.  A Written Authorisation for ESA funding from the National Delegation(s) is required for the Full Proposal.  How to apply  Visit the How to Apply to Proof-of-concept studies and Pilot Projects page for the full application details.  Proposals are assessed individually on a rolling, non-competitive basis; companies are therefore strongly encouraged to submit their APQ as early as possible.  Further information and important documentation can be found on the BASS documents page.

data.desc: The challenge  Environmental crime represents a critical global challenge that severely impacts ecosystems, public health, and the economy. It is now recognised as the world's fourth-largest criminal enterprise, generating up to €230 billion in annual global economic losses (UNEP-INTERPOL). This threat has driven a massive regulatory shift, marked by the enforcement of the EU’s Environmental Crime Directive and intensified global anti-greenwashing laws. Non-compliance can now trigger severe corporate penalties – reaching up to 10% of total global revenue – and expose executives to personal penalties.  Scope of the Funding Call  This opportunity supports the development of space-based applications and services targeting the following areas:   Integrity and corporate fraud: Greenwashing, falsified environmental certifications, and verifying carbon credit baselines. Poaching and wildlife: Illicit trade of protected species and endangered flora, and monitoring online black markets. Illegal fishing and marine activities: Dark vessel tracking, Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing, and maritime bilge dumping.  Illegal mining and quarrying: Unauthorised mineral extraction footprints, unpermitted sand mining and critical raw material tracing.  Waste and pollution: Illegal transboundary waste shipments, e-waste dumping, landfill expansions, chemical spills, and toxic emissions.
